name: Myobrace

lead: Myobrace is a brand of prefabricated myofunctional appliance made by Myofunctional Research Co. It is a soft-and-hard mouthpiece worn mostly while sleeping plus about an hour a day, intended to train the tongue and lips and encourage nasal breathing. The aim is straighter teeth and better jaw development, which would show in the smile and the facial profile.

The maker positions it as preventive treatment for children aged about 5 to 15. Studies, mostly in children, have compared it with the Twin Block appliance for Class II bites and reported changes in overjet and jaw position. Adults and teens use it in looksmaxxing circles hoping to move the jaw forward or keep teeth aligned after braces.

paras: The appliance is placed in the mouth for around an hour while awake and overnight, with different sizes and stages chosen for age and bite. Many users on forums combine it with tongue posture and nasal breathing habits. Treatment is typically measured in months to years, and the manufacturer directs patients to trained practitioners.

Reported downsides are temporary soreness and a need for consistent wear. Orthodontists note it works best during growth, and adult skeletal change is not documented in trials. Forum users have worried it could shift teeth straightened by braces. A study of Instagram posts found that claims about orthodontic products, Myobrace included, vary in how well they match research.

angle.text: In children the appliance is used to align teeth and correct bite problems such as overjet, which changes the smile and profile. Adult users hope for similar jaw and teeth effects, and some use it as a retainer after braces.

lead: Myobrace is a prefabricated myofunctional appliance from Myofunctional Research Co. that people wear to train the tongue, lips and breathing pattern while teeth and jaws are developing. The goal is straighter teeth and a better-balanced profile, achieved by changing the muscle forces acting on the arches rather than by pushing teeth with wires. [1][2]

The maker presents it as preventive pre-orthodontic treatment for children roughly 5 to 15, worn about an hour a day and during sleep, and says it is used by dental professionals in more than 100 countries. [3] Its description of the appliance is that a soft outer part acts like an archwire while a hard inner part engages the teeth individually. [4]

In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a way to 'project the mandible forward', improve overjet or act as a retainer; users also try it in adulthood. The published research is mostly in children and includes randomized trials, retrospective series and case reports. [5][6]

paras: Myobrace is sold in stages and sizes depending on the patient's age and bite. A published case report describes its structure as combining the dental alignment ability of rigid and soft appliances, with a soft outer part acting like the wire of a fixed appliance and a hard inner part engaging each tooth. [4]

The underlying idea of myofunctional therapy is that muscle behaviour of the lips, tongue and jaw shapes the relationship between the teeth and jaws, so correcting function can influence alignment. A 2023 review of electromyography in myofunctional orthodontics describes the mechanism as neuromuscular and skeletal adaptation to altered orofacial function. [2]

Forum users describe buying generic or branded versions, wearing them at night and for about an hour awake, and aiming to push the jaw forward, define the jawline or reduce overjet. One user reported a more defined jawline and changes in eyelid exposure within days, and others asked whether an adult needs a prescription. [7][8]

Users also ask whether it could disturb teeth straightened with braces; one poster wrote of fearing it would change teeth that cost money to straighten, while another described it as a better retainer. [9][7]

Orthodontic literature treats it as one of several functional appliances used during growth. Researchers note that the best outcomes for malocclusion treatment come when treatment occurs during childhood growth. [1]
A study of 300 Instagram posts about six marketed orthodontic products, including #myobrace, examined how claims in the posts compared with the research on those products. [10]

A 2024 systematic review of five studies comparing Myobrace with the Twin Block in Class II children reported that both appliances reduced overjet significantly, promoted mandibular growth and improved facial profile. [1]
A randomized trial of 26 children aged 9 to 12 compared Twin Block and Myobrace for effects on the pharyngeal airway over six months. [5]

A retrospective study of 60 adolescents found significant airway increases with Invisalign Mandibular Advancement, Myobrace and Twin Block, with the smallest change in the Myobrace group, and improvements in sagittal jaw measurements across all three. [11]

A 2025 study of children aged 6 to 10 reported improvements in alignment and crossbite across Class I, II and III cases, and a retrospective study of 30 Vietnamese children found it effective for anterior crossbite. [6][12]
A case report of a 9-year-old with Class II division 1 malocclusion described improved facial profile after 12 months. [4]

lore.intro: Myobrace threads on looksmax.org mix first-night reports, questions about purchase and age, and worries about adult use. [7][8]
